#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 4 -t 120h --job-name=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C --output=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_{id}.out --error=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_{id}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from original Slurm script)
# -n 4         : 4 tasks (for 4 GPU training)
# -g 4         : 4 GPUs total (from --gres=gpu:a100:4)
# -t 120h      : 120 hour walltime (from --time=120:0:0)
# --job-name=  : job name (from -J solov2-tissuenet-n-2C)
# --output=    : stdout redirection (from --output=%x_%j.out)
# --error=     : stderr redirection (from --error=%x_%j.err)
#
# Note: Flux uses {id} for job ID instead of %j, and job name must be embedded manually
# Note: GPU specification syntax differs - Flux uses -g for GPU count
# The specific GPU type (a100) cannot be directly specified in standard Flux
# GPU type selection depends on Flux configuration and available resources
#
# Alternative GPU allocation syntax if supported by your Flux instance:
# -o gpu-per-task=1 (would allocate 1 GPU per task with 4 tasks)
# -o gpus-per-node=4 (allocates 4 GPUs on the node)

# Original job name: solov2-tissuenet-n-2C
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C ...

# Original output/error files: %x_%j.out and %x_%j.err
# Set at submission with job name embedded in filename

# Account/Project: sada-cnmi
# Note: Flux uses banks/accounts through flux-accounting
# Set at submission: flux batch --setattr=bank=sada-cnmi ...
# Performance impact: Without bank specification, job may run under default account
# which could affect priority, resource limits, or accounting tracking

# Partition: tier3
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux queue policies
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Memory requirement: 200G
# Note: Memory requests in Flux can be specified at submission time
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory=200G
# Or use flux resource constraint syntax based on your Flux version
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# GPU Type: a100
# Note: Flux GPU allocation does not support specifying GPU model in standard syntax
# GPU type/model selection depends on Flux resource graph configuration
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated different GPU types if available
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property constraints

spack load cuda@11.0.2%gcc@9.3.0/lrd2rcw
cd mmdetection
nvidia-smi

# Original command uses 4 processes for distributed training
# In Flux context, if using MPI-based distribution, consider:
# flux run -n 4 -g 1 python ... (would launch 4 tasks, each with 1 GPU)
# However, preserving original shell script approach for compatibility
sh mmdetection/tools/dist_train.sh mmdetection/configs/solov22C/solov2_r50_fpn_60e_coco_tissuenet_n.py 4 --work-dir /shared/rc/spl/mmdet_output/All_to_all/nuclear/SOLOv2

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

Memory requirement (200G) from original Slurm script is not included in the documented submission command. The comment mentions using '--setattr=system.memory=200G' but this is not included in the main submission command example. This could lead to OOM errors if the default memory allocation is insufficient.

The recommended submission command should be updated to: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 4 -t 120h --setattr=system.memory=200G --setattr=bank=sada-cnmi --job-name=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C --output=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_{id}.out --error=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_{id}.err script.sh'
The output/error filename pattern uses '{id}' which should be verified for the specific Flux version. Some versions may use '{{id}}' or '{{jobid}}' instead of '{id}'.

The '-g 4' flag allocates 4 GPUs total, which combined with '-n 4' (4 tasks) may not guarantee 1 GPU per task. Using '-o gpu-per-task=1' with '-n 4' would be more explicit for distributed training scenarios.

The script documentation mentions alternative GPU allocation syntax but doesn't provide clear guidance on which approach to use. For distributed deep learning with 4 GPUs, the submission should ideally use either: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 4' or 'flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -o gpu-per-task=1' depending on the Flux configuration.

The 'cd mmdetection' command changes directory, but if the script fails before this point, the working directory assumption may cause issues. Consider using absolute paths or verifying directory existence.

The shell script 'mmdetection/tools/dist_train.sh' is called directly with 'sh', which assumes the distributed training script handles GPU assignment internally. In a Flux environment, it may be better to use 'flux run' to launch the distributed training processes to ensure proper GPU binding.
No validation check exists for whether the required 4 GPUs are actually available before attempting to run the training script.
